title: Hub reportAbuse: canReportAbuse for reportingUser (role 0 if absent or unlisted), reportingUser domain must be From, 403 report-not-allowed
description:
protocol-07 §5.9 says nothing about authorizing a report; room-policy-04 §8.3 defines canReportAbuse ('the holder can report a franked instant message as abusive') but not who checks it or against which identity. §5.9 makes reportingUser optional (empty means absent, decision mimid-1wgh.5.59) and the hub sees only the From provider.

Readings: (a) do not check (the previous state, decision mimid-1wgh.21); (b) check the From provider only, which has no role; (c) check reportingUser's role; for an empty or unlisted reportingUser, role 0 (room-policy-04 §8: role 0 is the role of a non-participant).

Chosen (c). The hub's single policy point (hub/policy.rs authorize_report_abuse) refuses a banned user and requires canReportAbuse of the role; in an open room (no base_room_policy, decision mimid-1wgh.52) a listed participant holds every capability and role 0 none, as for every other check. A non-empty reportingUser's domain must be the From domain, a consistency check as for sendingUri in submitMessage (decision mimid-1wgh.6.9), so a provider cannot borrow another provider's user's role; this reverses the old Limitation 'From is not compared with reportingUser'. The policy check runs before any frank is verified. A refusal is HTTP 403 with problem type report-not-allowed (§5.9: the code only says whether the report was accepted; 422 stays for an unverifiable message, decision mimid-1wgh.6.65). INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC: the 403 and its problem type.
notes: 2026-11-19: the canReportAbuse check still runs first, before frank verification and before the unverified_abusive_messages component (decision mimid-1wgh.60) is read.
